title: The Ball That Goes Away
setting: a long park path: a bench on the left and a second bench far off to the right (about 14 m apart), both in the back layer, with a tree or two between them.
shots: A stick man is sitting on the left bench, facing the front. A red ball lies on the bench beside him.
Still sitting, the man looks at the ball. Only when his look ends does the ball start rolling to the right along the bench; it falls off the end, bounces on the ground and keeps rolling to the right.

The man stands up and runs after the ball to the right. The ball stays only about 2 m ahead of him for most of the chase, so both are in the shot together; near the end it speeds up, gets away far to the right past the second bench and leaves the shot.
The man slows from the run to a normal walk for a few steps, stops, then walks sadly the rest of the way to the second bench and sits down on it facing the front.
The ball rolls back in from the right and stops on the ground right in front of him.
The man stands up and looks down at the ball. Only when his look ends does the ball start rolling again; it rolls away to the left out of sight.
camera: follow the man the whole time, framed about 9 m wide so the ball stays in view during the chase until it gets away; keep the camera steady while he sits.
